verses.commentary: Return, Israel, to the Lord your God. The final call. After all the judgment, still an invitation. Your sins have been your downfall. The diagnosis clear. But return is possible.

Take words with you and return to the Lord. Not sacrifices but speech. Say to him: Forgive all our sins. The prayer for pardon. Receive us graciously. Appeal to grace. That we may offer the fruit of our lips. Words of praise replace animal sacrifice. Hebrews 13:15 echoes this.

Assyria cannot save us. Renouncing political trust. We will not mount warhorses. Renouncing military trust. We will never again say Our gods to what our own hands have made. Renouncing idolatry. For in you the fatherless find compassion. Trust placed rightly. Orphans, the most vulnerable, find care in God.
I will heal their waywardness. Divine response to true repentance. And love them freely. Grace upon grace. For my anger has turned away from them. Wrath satisfied. The father welcomes the prodigal.

I will be like the dew to Israel. Gentle, life-giving moisture. He will blossom like a lily. Beautiful flowering. Like a cedar of Lebanon he will send down his roots. Deep stability. Contrasting images: delicate flower, mighty tree.
His young shoots will grow. Expansion. His splendor will be like an olive tree. Productive beauty. His fragrance like a cedar of Lebanon. Pleasant presence. The restored Israel flourishes.

People will dwell again in his shade. Providing shelter for others. They will flourish like the grain. Abundant harvest. They will blossom like the vine. Fruitful growth. Israel's fame will be like the wine of Lebanon. Renowned excellence.

Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? Final renunciation. I will answer him and care for him. God's committed response. I am like a flourishing juniper. God as evergreen tree. Your fruitfulness comes from me. The source of all blessing declared. Not idols, not self, but God.

Who is wise? Let them realize these things. Challenge to readers. Who is discerning? Let them understand. The book demands response. The ways of the Lord are right. Divine paths validated. The righteous walk in them. The faithful follow. But the rebellious stumble in them. The same paths that guide the righteous trip the wicked. The book ends with choice: wisdom or rebellion, life or stumbling.
